stage: Stage 2 - PLAN ONLY, do not build in this task
description: Cover art: real box art for every game, with a fallback that is never blank. The user raised this twice and specifically: the old prototype 'had ways to pull cover art' and the library 'needs to have the art of the game'. The browser build DID have a full five-tier artwork system and it is still in the tree as the design source, so this is a port of a solved problem and not a new design. THE RECOMMENDATION IS TO SHIP REAL BOX ART, NOT ONLY PLACEHOLDERS, and the iOS version is strictly easier than the browser one for a reason worth knowing.

decision_point.question: Where does cover art come from, given the app is handed nothing but a filename and some bytes?
decision_point.what_the_browser_did: Five tiers, documented in web/src/data/artwork.js: (1) libretro Named_Boxarts, (2) libretro Named_Titles and Named_Snaps, (3) the same with tags stripped, (4) an in-game capture past frame 60, (5) a file the user picked. Anything with no art at all fell through to a procedural console-themed plate (web/src/ui/art.js), which is why no card was ever blank. docs/mobile-after.png shows that fallback plate in use: a coloured gradient with a letter, which is the state to improve on rather than the target.
decision_point.the_constraint_that_shaped_the_browser_v: thumbnails.libretro.com sends NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. Verified in web/src/data/boxart.js rather than assumed: fetch in cors mode is refused, no-cors yields an opaque response whose status is always 0 so it cannot even distinguish a hit from a miss, and drawing the image into a canvas taints it. So the browser could only probe with objects and persist the resolved URL, never the bytes. The file says plainly that scraped art is therefore not guaranteed offline.
decision_point.why_ios_is_better_and_this_is_the_key_in: CORS is a browser policy. URLSession has no such restriction, so the iOS app can download the actual PNG bytes, store them in Caches or Application Support, and show real box art fully offline. The tier that was the browser's weakest becomes the strongest. Do not port the probe workaround: it exists only to work around a restriction that does not apply here.
decision_point.recommendation: Implement tiers 1 to 3 against the libretro thumbnail server with URLSession, storing real bytes on disk; keep the procedural plate as the never-blank fallback and as the loading state behind a decoding image; add tier 5 (a user-picked file) because it is cheap once the store exists and is the only answer for a ROM the database has never heard of; defer tier 4 (in-game capture) because it needs a framebuffer readback that is not exposed through UniFFI today. Ship it OFF-BY-DEFAULT-VISIBLE but ON: that is, fetch art by default, but put the switch in Settings and say what it does, because resolving art sends the ROM's filename to a third party. The browser build treated that as a real disclosure rather than an implementation detail and so should this one.

steps: Add a `SystemArtwork` catalogue mapping each GameSystem to its libretro playlist directory name. These are NOT guessable and every one was checked against the live server for the browser build, so copy them from web/src/data/boxart.js LIBRETRO_DIRS rather than inventing them: nes 'Nintendo - Nintendo Entertainment System', snes 'Nintendo - Super Nintendo Entertainment System', gb 'Nintendo - Game Boy', gbc 'Nintendo - Game Boy Color', gba 'Nintendo - Game Boy Advance', sms 'Sega - Master System - Mark III', genesis 'Sega - Mega Drive - Genesis', ps1 'Sony - PlayStation'. Note the two traps: Master System is 'Mark III' suffixed, and Game Gear has NO entry in the browser table, so gg needs 'Sega - Game Gear' added and confirmed against the server before it is trusted.

Port the filename to thumbnail-name transform exactly. It is a SUBSTITUTION and not a strip: the characters & * / : ` < > ? \ | " each become a single underscore so 'Ratchet & Clank' becomes 'Ratchet _ Clank' with both spaces intact. Removing the character instead yields a double space and never matches. Then the three name forms, most specific first: the exact base name; the name with only [square bracket] dump tags dropped; the name with every (..) and [..] tag dropped. The middle form earns its place and the order matters: libretro names follow No-Intro, which uses parenthesised regions, so stripping everything first turns 'Super Mario World (USA) [!]' into 'Super Mario World', which 404s, when 'Super Mario World (USA)' is a 200.

Build the candidate ladder name-major, not folder-major: for each name form, try Named_Boxarts then Named_Titles then Named_Snaps. An exact-name box art is by far the commonest outcome, so the common case costs one request and only a genuine miss walks all nine. Skip a name form that reduced to nothing or duplicates one already tried, which is what stops a tag-free title such as 'Tetris (World)' costing three wasted requests.

Fetch with URLSession and store the bytes. A URLSession data task with a HEAD or a ranged GET can distinguish a hit from a miss honestly, unlike the browser's probe, and a 404 from this server returns text/html so the content type is worth checking before trusting a 200. Write each hit into a dedicated artwork directory keyed on a hash of the entry path, not into Documents, because Documents is user-visible through the Files app and artwork is not user content.
Cap concurrency at 3, as the browser did. Importing thirty ROMs would otherwise open up to 270 connections, and the radio and the memory are better spent on the game the user is waiting for.

Keep the negative cache. A total miss is remembered with a timestamp and not retried for a week, because the libretro repository gains thumbnails over time so a permanent miss would be wrong, and re-probing nine URLs per unknown ROM on every launch would be worse. Store it in UserDefaults, which is the native peer of the localStorage the browser used.

Port the procedural plate as the never-blank fallback: FNV-1a over the title plus the entry id, the system anchoring the hue so every Game Boy plate lands in the same green family and a shelf reads as a set, and one of five gradient patterns chosen by the hash. Reproduce it as a SwiftUI LinearGradient / RadialGradient / AngularGradient rather than as CSS. The hues from web/src/data/systems.js: nes 355, snes 268, gb 88, gbc 45, gba 200, sms 18, genesis 220, ps1 240, and gg needs a hue choosing since the browser had no Game Gear entry.
Draw real art OVER the plate rather than instead of it, which makes the plate the loading state for a cover that has not decoded and the letterbox behind one that does not fill its box.

Add tier 5: a user-picked image, through the same picker discipline the import flow already proved (a strongly retained delegate, because the picker's delegate property is weak). Reuse that machinery rather than writing a second picker path.

Record tier 4 (in-game capture past frame 60, 512x384) as deferred and say why: it needs a framebuffer readback exported through UniFFI, which is a Rust change. The browser had it and it is genuinely nice, because it is the only tier that works for a ROM no database knows.

Put the artwork switch in Settings (FEAT-005) with a sentence saying that resolving art sends the ROM filename to thumbnails.libretro.com, plus a 'clear artwork cache' action and a 'retry failed lookups' action that clears the negative cache.
acceptance_criteria: A library card for a commercially named ROM shows its real box art, downloaded once and shown from disk afterwards with no network.
A ROM with no art on the server shows a deterministic console-themed plate, never a blank or a broken-image box, and the same plate every launch.
The filename transform substitutes rather than strips, and the three name forms are tried in the documented order.
At most 3 artwork requests are in flight at once.
A miss is not retried for a week, and Settings can clear that.
Artwork is stored outside Documents so it never appears in the Files app as user content.
Nothing blocks the library from appearing: art resolves asynchronously and a card renders immediately on its plate.
The artwork switch, what it discloses, and the cache actions are all in Settings.
Game Gear's libretro directory name is confirmed against the live server before it is trusted, because the browser table had no entry for it.
verification: Unit-testable without a network and worth testing that way: the filename transform, the three name forms, the candidate ladder order and the plate's hash-to-gradient choice are all pure functions. If a Swift test target is added, these are the first things in it.
By eye against web/src/data/boxart.js: the directory names, the invalid character set, the two strip functions and the ladder order.
On device: a real ROM resolving real art, an obscure ROM falling back to a plate, and art surviving a relaunch in airplane mode.
Confirm the Game Gear directory name with a single request before shipping it.
findings: Not implemented in this task, by scope. Recorded here because the user asked about it twice and because the answer is already in the repository: the browser build's five-tier system is intact in web/src/data/boxart.js, web/src/data/artwork.js and web/src/ui/art.js, and web/ is dead scaffolding that must not be edited but is explicitly still the design reference. The single most useful finding is that the constraint which crippled the browser version does not exist on iOS: thumbnails.libretro.com sends no CORS header, which is why the browser could only probe with and persist a URL, but URLSession is not bound by CORS, so iOS can store the real bytes and show real box art offline. Porting the probe workaround would be copying a scar.
